title: Levites numbered “from thirty years old” — the Greek of the same verses says twenty-five
summary: Seven verses of Numbers 4 in the KJV, with the Hebrew, number the Levites for the work of the tabernacle “from thirty years old”. Brenton’s Greek has “from twenty-five” in every one of them, which is the age the KJV itself gives at Numbers 8:24.
text: KJV Numbers 4:3: “From thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old” KJV 4:23: “From thirty years old and upward until fifty years old shalt thou number them” KJV 4:30, 4:35, 4:39, 4:43 and 4:47 each have: “From thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old” KJV 8:24: “from twenty and five years old and upward they shall go in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation” Hebrew (WLC) 4:3: מִבֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה [from a son of thirty years and upward]. 8:24: מִבֶּן֩ חָמֵ֨שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה [from a son of five and twenty years and upward]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 4:3: ἀπὸ εἴκοσι καὶ πέντε ἐτῶν καὶ ἐπάνω ἕως πεντήκοντα ἐτῶν [from twenty-five years and upward until fifty years]. 4:23, 4:30, 4:35, 4:39, 4:43 and 4:47 each have: ἀπὸ πέντε καὶ εἰκοσαετοῦς καὶ ἐπάνω ἕως πεντηκονταετοῦς [from twenty-five years old and upward until fifty years old]. 8:24: ἀπὸ πέντε καὶ εἰκοσαετοῦς καὶ ἐπάνω [from twenty-five years old and upward]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/4/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/8/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM04.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM08.htm.
reasoning: In the KJV and the Hebrew quoted, the numbering in chapter 4 starts at thirty and the rule in chapter 8 starts at twenty-five. In Brenton’s Greek the starting age is twenty-five in both chapters, so the two chapters do not differ in that edition.
scope: G applies at Numbers 4:3, 4:23, 4:30, 4:35, 4:39, 4:43 and 4:47, where the Greek number differs from the KJV. At 8:24 the Greek agrees with the KJV and no tag applies there. title: Two alarms, for the east and south camps — the Greek adds a third and a fourth

title: The seventy elders “prophesied, and did not cease” — the Hebrew and the Greek say they did not do it again
summary: The KJV says the seventy elders prophesied “and did not cease”. The pointed Hebrew says they prophesied “and did not add”, and Brenton’s Greek says “and no longer added”: they did it then and not again. The KJV renders the same Hebrew verb at Deuteronomy 5:22 as “added no more”.
text: KJV Numbers 11:25: “and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:25: וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יָסָֽפוּ [and they prophesied and did not add]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 11:25: καὶ ἐπροφήτευσαν, καὶ οὐκ ἔτι προσέθεντο [and they prophesied, and no longer added]. KJV Deuteronomy 5:22: “with a great voice: and he added no more” Hebrew (WLC) Deuteronomy 5:22: קֹ֥ול גָּדֹ֖ול וְלֹ֣א יָסָ֑ף [a great voice, and he did not add]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Deuteronomy 5:22: φωνὴ μεγάλη· καὶ οὐ προσέθηκε [a great voice; and he did not add]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/11/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/5/5/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM11.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/DEU05.htm.
reasoning: The verb in the pointed Hebrew is the verb “to add” with a negative, the same form the KJV renders “he added no more” at Deuteronomy 5:22, where it means the speaking stopped. Brenton’s Greek uses its own verb “to add” in both verses. On that wording the elders prophesied when the spirit rested on them and did not go on. The KJV says the opposite about how long it lasted: they “did not cease”.
scope: H and G both apply at Numbers 11:25: the Greek agrees with the pointed Hebrew against the KJV. Deuteronomy 5:22 is quoted only to show how the KJV renders the same verb form; no tag applies there. The Hebrew consonants of the verb, without the vowel points, have also been read as a different verb meaning “come to an end”, which with the negative gives the KJV’s sense; the pointed Leningrad text and Brenton’s Greek do not read it that way. title: “He shall pour the water out of his buckets … higher than Agag” — the Greek has a man who rules many nations, and Gog
summary: In the KJV, with the Hebrew, Balaam’s oracle speaks of water poured from buckets, seed in many waters, and a king higher than Agag. Brenton’s Greek has no water: a man comes out of Israel’s seed and is lord of many nations, and the name in the next line is Gog.
text: KJV Numbers 24:7: “He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters, and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” Hebrew (WLC) 24:7: יִֽזַּל־מַ֙יִם֙ מִדָּ֣לְיָ֔ו וְזַרְעֹ֖ו בְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים וְיָרֹ֤ם מֵֽאֲגַג֙ מַלְכֹּ֔ו וְתִנַּשֵּׂ֖א מַלְכֻתֹֽו [water flows from his buckets, and his seed is in many waters; and his king is higher than Agag, and his kingdom is lifted up]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 24:7: Ἐξελεύσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ κυριεύσει ἐθνῶν πολλῶν· καὶ ὑψωθήσεται ἡ Γὼγ βασιλεία, καὶ αὐξηθήσεται βασιλεία αὐτοῦ [A man shall come out of his seed, and he shall be lord of many nations; and the kingdom of Gog shall be raised up, and his kingdom shall be increased]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/24/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM24.htm.
reasoning: The first half of the verse is a picture of water in the KJV and the Hebrew quoted, and a prediction of a man who is lord of many nations in Brenton’s Greek. In the second half the KJV names Agag and the Greek as printed names Gog.
scope: G applies at Numbers 24:7. This compares two published wordings of a poem and does not say which is original. The water in the KJV may be a figure for descendants or plenty, and so may be nearer to the Greek in sense than in words; the record shows what each text prints. How Gog stands to the kingdom in the Greek clause is not decided here; the bracket follows the words in the order printed. Who Agag and Gog are is not stated in the verse. title: “A Sceptre shall rise out of Israel” — in the Greek, “a man”

title: Kadesh: in the wilderness of Zin, or of Paran? The Greek of the journey list says Paran
summary: The KJV places Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran when the spies return, and in the wilderness of Zin in three later verses. In the list of journeys the KJV, with the Hebrew, says “the wilderness of Zin, which is Kadesh”. Brenton’s Greek adds a stage there and says “the wilderness of Pharan; this is Kades”.
text: KJV Numbers 13:26: “unto the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh” KJV 20:1: “into the desert of Zin in the first month: and the people abode in Kadesh” KJV 27:14: “that is the water of Meribah in Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin” KJV 33:36: “And they removed from Eziongaber, and pitched in the wilderness of Zin, which is Kadesh.” Hebrew (WLC) 13:26: אֶל־מִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָ֖ן קָדֵ֑שָׁה [to the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh]. 33:36: וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ בְמִדְבַּר־צִ֖ן הִ֥וא קָדֵֽשׁ [and they encamped in the wilderness of Zin; it is Kadesh]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 13:26: εἰς τὴν ἔρημον Φαρὰν Κάδης [to the wilderness of Pharan, Kades]. 33:36: καὶ παρενέβαλον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ Σίν· καὶ ἀπῇραν ἐκ τῆς ἐρήμου Σὶν, καὶ παρενέβαλον εἰς τὴν ἔρημον Φαράν· αὕτη ἐστὶ Κάδης [and they encamped in the wilderness of Sin; and they set out from the wilderness of Sin and encamped in the wilderness of Pharan; this is Kades]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/13/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/33/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM13.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM33.htm.
reasoning: At Numbers 33:36 the KJV and the Hebrew quoted identify Kadesh with the wilderness of Zin. Brenton’s Greek has one more stage in the same verse and identifies Kadesh with the wilderness of Pharan. The KJV itself has Kadesh in Paran at 13:26 and in Zin at 20:1, 27:14 and 33:36.
scope: G applies at Numbers 33:36 only; at 13:26 the Greek agrees with the KJV. The KJV’s two placings clash as worded but can be reconciled in ways the text does not report: Kadesh may have lain where the two wildernesses met, one wilderness may have been counted part of the other, or two visits or two places may be meant. This record does not decide between them, and does not say whether the Greek’s extra stage is original. No H is proposed: the KJV follows the Hebrew. title: Who met Israel at Hormah, and from where: Amalekites and Canaanites of the valley, Canaanites of the hill, or Amorites of the mountain?
summary: Numbers 14:25 says the Amalekites and the Canaanites dwelt in the valley. Twenty verses later the Amalekites come down with “the Canaanites which dwelt in that hill”. Deuteronomy tells the same defeat and names neither people: it was “the Amorites, which dwelt in that mountain”.
text: KJV Numbers 14:25: “(Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites dwelt in the valley.)” KJV 14:43: “For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you” KJV 14:45: “Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites which dwelt in that hill, and smote them, and discomfited them, even unto Hormah.” KJV Deuteronomy 1:44: “And the Amorites, which dwelt in that mountain, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and destroyed you in Seir, even unto Hormah.” Hebrew (WLC) Numbers 14:25: וְהָֽעֲמָלֵקִ֥י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יֹושֵׁ֣ב בָּעֵ֑מֶק [and the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valley]. 14:45: וַיֵּ֤רֶד הָעֲמָלֵקִי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב בָּהָ֣ר הַה֑וּא [and the Amalekite came down, and the Canaanite who dwells in that hill country]. Deuteronomy 1:44: וַיֵּצֵ֨א הָאֱמֹרִ֜י הַיֹּשֵׁ֨ב בָּהָ֤ר הַהוּא֙ [and the Amorite who dwells in that hill country came out]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Numbers 14:25: Ὁ δὲ Ἀμαλὴκ καὶ ὁ Χαναναῖος κατοικοῦσιν ἐν τῇ κοιλάδι [and Amalek and the Canaanite dwell in the valley]. 14:45: Καὶ κατέβη ὁ Ἀμαλὴκ καὶ ὁ Χαναναῖος ὁ ἐνκαθήμενος ἐν τῷ ὄρει ἐκείνῳ [and Amalek came down, and the Canaanite who was settled in that mountain]. Deuteronomy 1:44: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ Ἀμοῤῥαῖος ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν τῷ ὄρει ἐκείνῳ [and the Amorite who dwells in that mountain came out]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/14/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/5/1/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM14.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/DEU01.htm.
reasoning: Two things differ as worded. First the place: the Canaanites “dwelt in the valley” in Numbers 14:25 and “dwelt in that hill” in 14:45, and they “came down” on Israel. Second the people: Numbers names Amalekites and Canaanites; Deuteronomy, telling the same defeat as far as Hormah, names Amorites and no one else. The Hebrew and Brenton’s Greek quoted have the same words as the KJV in all three verses.
scope: No tag is proposed: the Hebrew and Brenton’s Greek agree with the KJV. The statements clash as worded but can be reconciled in ways the text does not report: some Canaanites may have lived in the valley and others in the hill country; “the valley” of 14:25 may be a different district from the hill of 14:45; and “Amorites” may be used in Deuteronomy as a general name for the peoples of the hill country. This record sets the wordings side by side and does not decide between those readings. The Hebrew word rendered “hill” in Numbers and “mountain” in Deuteronomy is the same word; that difference is not part of the finding. title: When was Hormah named: when Israel under Moses destroyed the Canaanites, or when Judah and Simeon destroyed Zephath?
summary: In Numbers, Israel in the wilderness destroys the Canaanites and their cities, and the place is called Hormah. In Judges, Judah and Simeon destroy the Canaanite city of Zephath, and the city is called Hormah. The name is already used in Numbers 14:45, before either naming.
text: KJV Numbers 14:45: “and smote them, and discomfited them, even unto Hormah” KJV 21:2: “then I will utterly destroy their cities” KJV 21:3: “And the Lord hearkened to the voice of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites; and they utterly destroyed them and their cities: and he called the name of the place Hormah.” KJV Judges 1:17: “And Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they slew the Canaanites that inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. And the name of the city was called Hormah.” Hebrew (WLC) Numbers 21:3: וַיִּקְרָ֥א שֵׁם־הַמָּקֹ֖ום חָרְמָֽה [and he called the name of the place Hormah]. Judges 1:17: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שֵׁם־הָעִ֖יר חָרְמָֽה [and he called the name of the city Hormah]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Numbers 21:3: καὶ ἐπεκάλεσαν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου, Ἀνάθεμα [and they called the name of that place Anathema]. Judges 1:17: καὶ ἐκάλεσε τὸ ὄνομα τῆς πόλεως, Ἀνάθεμα [and he called the name of the city Anathema]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/21/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/7/1/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/NUM21.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JDG01.htm.
reasoning: Each passage tells of Canaanites utterly destroyed and of the name Hormah being given because of it. They put the naming in different times and under different leaders: all Israel in the wilderness in Numbers, Judah with Simeon in Judges. Read as worded, the same name is given for the same reason twice.
scope: No tag is proposed. The Hebrew of both verses has the name as the KJV has it. Brenton’s Greek translates the name in both verses with the same word, so it does not side with either account; that the Greek translates a name the KJV transliterates is noted, not tagged. The two can be reconciled in ways the text does not report: Numbers says “the place” and Judges “the city”, so two places may be meant; the same site may have been destroyed and named twice; or one account may tell ahead of time what the other tells in its place. The use of the name at Numbers 14:45 may be the narrator’s later name for the place. This record does not decide between those readings.
